outcome: Prevalence of symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse
cohort: Primiparous women who delivered between 1985 and 1988 and had no further deliveries
finding: The late prevalence of urinary incontinence, symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse, and fecal incontinence was similar between vacuum extraction and spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Vacuum extraction almost tripled the rate of obstetric anal sphincter injury compared with spontaneous vaginal delivery, and obstetric anal sphincter injury after vacuum extraction substantially increased the prevalence of fecal incontinence and urinary incontinence but did not alter the rate of symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse.
